answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring every new identity to stake a rising amount of onyx-backed collateral into a shared trellis of mutual bonds. Each bond locks until the next dawn, and the stake curve doubles per additional head under the same operator key. An attacker forging ten clones pays 1024x the base stake in locked capital that cannot be recycled until unlock, while an honest agent pays once. The trellis verifies the unique operator signature on each bond, so shared capital fails the check and the cost makes mass fabrication uneconomic.
